KROWNLANDIA COMMUNITY LIBRARY · NOVEMBER 5, 2026

Krownlandia: Yet to build

A proposed development sequence for residents, guests and creators. This list separates the current prototype from future shared services and new platforms.

Already built: browser exploration, rides, lounges, homes, local rewards and keepsakes, progress backups, personal points-over-time, a calendar framework and photo/video capture.
Still future work: shared multiplayer presence, account-synchronized rewards, a public verified leaderboard, visitor activity auditing and a Unity version.

Recreation inventory: which activity fits first?

Version 281 has the Great Journey and Safari rides, a village tram and a giant-tree Clubhouse meeting room. Those experiences provide travel, viewpoints and board activities. None supplies a controllable race vehicle, a sports field, a golf hole or a bowling lane. The following comparisons use the existing PDF inventory; names and credits describe historical ideas only.

  • Krown Bowling (page 10, @mariromero22): a single practice rack can work with text, ordinary buttons and no additional 3D space. Selected for the first recreation prototype.
  • Olympic Stadium (page 10, @elizabeths14), Baseball Stadium, Soccer Stadium and Race Track (page 10, @DanGyver): the existing ride paths do not establish any of these venues. Defer field layout, vehicle controls and competitive play.
  • Krownlandia Pines and Bluffs Golf Courses (page 11): neither course has a playable hole. The separate page-14 condo and house entries credit @lisachandler; the inventory lists no credit on the two course entries. Defer course footprints and preserve existing homes.

Implemented: one untimed bowling rack

The Park map offers a collapsed tabletop practice card, separate from walking destinations. Start with ten numbered pins. Choose Left (2, 4, 7, 8), Center (1, 2, 3, 5) or Right (3, 6, 9, 10), then roll. Only standing pins in that group fall. A second roll ends the rack, even if it hits no pins. Show the standing pin numbers and roll count in text. Restart restores the rack. These rules and the card location are new design choices, not historical details or regulation bowling.

Acceptance: Verify Center then Left leaves 6, 9 and 10 standing; repeating Center leaves six pins and uses both rolls. Disable a third roll. Support keyboard-only choice, roll and restart without a timer or pointer aim. Closing and reopening starts fresh and returns focus to the opener. No map guidance, scene objects, animation, audio, purchases, progress writes, leaderboard or shared play. The tabletop interpretation is now implemented. Live browser and assistive-technology reviews remain paused.

Outdoor recreation: fishing from the Riverbend bank

The page-3 village description connects fishing to Riverbend. Its existing river, railed path, discovery display and lantern-boat bench give visitors a place to try a cast without entering the water. Open the display, or use the bench’s View options → Read Riverbend stories, then choose Try a riverside cast. Cast near the bank or into the current and reel in at your own pace. The text describes the float and its wake; these are new practice scenes. No catch, points or saved collection.

Still proposed: A Pool (@AmineU, page 12), Aqua Discovery (@kyriakos, page 13), Blee Fish (@ajayblee, page 13) and Gotham’s Beach (@Jauregui9821, page 15) are separate entries. The river and its bridge do not establish any of those venues or authorize attributing their designs to the Riverbend activity.

Longer-term milestones

1. Test the visitor experience · Paused

Resume prerequisite: Lisa resumes the review project and a controllable WebGL-capable browser is available. Tester access is already verified. Then conduct an authorized walkthrough of entry/resume, navigation, seating, panel obstruction, day/night appearance and camera recording. Check desktop and small-screen controls, keyboard access and supported browsers.

Completion check: reproduce and prioritize findings, fix blocking issues, and record which real-browser behaviors were verified. Keep existing saves and backups intact.

2. Establish shared identity and services

Choose account identity, visitor display names and roles for guests, residents, place managers, administrators and agents. Decide what visitors can use without an account. Separate display credits such as “place manager” from actual permissions.

Design persistent server storage and an authenticated API with explicit ownership checks. Plan account recovery, data export, deletion and retention. Define which activities are logged and show visitors a clear notice before enabling tracking.

Completion check: two test accounts cannot access each other's private data, roles are enforced on the server, and recovery/export flows work.

3. Add server-verified rewards tracking

Keep the existing browser points as legacy local progress. Build a server-owned reward ledger recording account, station/activity, reward amount, server time and a unique claim identifier. Validate completion and eligibility on the server; make retries idempotent so repeated requests cannot award duplicate points.

Design reconciliation and backup migration deliberately: imported local scores must not become verified competitive scores merely because a client submits them. Preserve existing keepsakes and label historical, unverified totals clearly. Separate ordinary reward events from administrator adjustments and retain an audit trail for corrections.

Completion check: simultaneous claims, retries, offline/reconnect cases and manipulated client timestamps cannot duplicate or invent verified points.

4. Pilot multiplayer in one small area

Begin with a limited Town Square session where two invited test visitors can see each other's avatar and movement. Choose a real-time transport and hosting approach after testing latency, reconnect behavior, capacity and costs. Synchronize only the state needed for presence at first; keep the full park available as a single-player experience.

Define spawn points, session limits, disconnect cleanup, visibility choices and agent identification. Establish block/report and moderation behavior before adding chat or user-generated content. Decide separately whether seats, housing and activities are shared or instanced.

Completion check: visitors join, move, disconnect and reconnect predictably without losing local progress or gaining unauthorized control over another visitor.

5. Add leaderboards and useful administration

Once verified reward data exists, introduce opt-in hourly, daily, monthly, yearly and all-time rankings. Define Pacific-time boundaries, ties, privacy choices, corrections and anti-abuse rules. Keep legacy points separate from verified rankings.

Expand the current publication-only admin log to approved visitor/agent activity events. Show actor type, event, time and outcome with role-limited access. Avoid collecting chat, recordings or detailed movement by default; decide the minimum events needed and their retention.

Completion check: rankings derive from the server ledger, timezone boundaries and corrections are tested, and visitors can understand what is visible to others.

6. Build a Unity proof of concept

Start with one small scene - for example, the gate and Lisa's Coffee Shop - rather than attempting to convert the entire world at once. Choose target devices, rendering requirements and a supported Unity setup after reviewing current platform capabilities, terms and costs.

The current JavaScript/Three.js application is not already a Unity project. Plan to recreate or port scene geometry, materials, controls and interactions; review asset rights and performance. Maintain shared place IDs, reward definitions and documented save schemas.

Connect the Unity client to the same authenticated identity and reward services as the browser version. Neither client should be trusted to award points. Test control parity, seating, accessible UI, networking and save migration before expanding.

Completion check: a visitor completes one equivalent activity in each client, sees consistent verified progress, and can return to the browser version without losing data. A full Unity world, cross-play and VR remain later decisions.

7. Continue community-led world building

Craft discovery · November 6: Park map → Craft activities now gathers five implemented practice destinations: Meadowbrook weaving and market arranging, Riverbend pottery/baskets, Eldergrove woodcraft and Stonehearth stone patterns (added November 13). Results provide walking directions and explain where to open each activity. Practice designs last until reload and add no points or saved keepsakes. Live visual/accessibility review remains unverified.

Review remaining original-document ideas against what is already built. Expand established villages only with verified source descriptions and credits. Confirm the Sunvale/Sunnyvale naming ambiguity before using it as a new village label. Publish actual events only after Lisa confirms their details.

Assess the living simulation and sticker artwork as separate integrations, including permissions and technical feasibility. Existing outbound links do not provide embedded simulation, shared accounts or imported emoji assets.

Royal Plaza Fountain: can visitors choose still water?

November 14 · source review of version 274. At that time, no. Detailed, Balanced and Lightweight adjust resolution and shadows. All three keep the same spray: one mesh containing 240 drops. On each rendered frame the park rewrites all 240 positions and scales, even when the fountain is outside the view. Hidden tabs and lost graphics contexts skip this work. This describes the code; frame rate and visitor comfort have not been measured.

The device’s reduced-motion preference makes the day/night lighting change immediate. It does not stop the water. The twelve small lights around the rim respond to the day/night blend; they are not a timed light show. The existing Royal Plaza Fountain station grants its 25-point night task for visiting after dark. Watching the spray is not a condition.

Available now: still water

Open Graphics → Royal Plaza Fountain spray. “Follow device motion setting” hides the spray when reduced motion is enabled, including when the device setting changes during a visit. Choose “Keep water still” to hide it regardless of that setting. The basin, tiers, lights, audio and 25-point night visit remain independent. The choice is remembered on this device when browser storage is available and is separate from progress backups.

Deterministic scene checks cover all three quality profiles, live motion changes, 240 spray writes per moving frame and zero per still frame, and single-claim night rewards. Actual rendering, GPU performance and assistive technology remain unverified.

Separate historical idea: Dancing Fountain (@thebrainchild0x, PDF page 15). The inventory supplies the name and credit. See the prototype brief. The local prototype is available; no historical choreography, event date or permission is inferred.

Dancing Fountain · visitor experience

Implemented · November 14. The inventory records “Dancing Fountain” and @thebrainchild0x on PDF page 15. The three water patterns below are new prototype ideas. The prototype lets one visitor try them at the existing Royal Plaza Fountain without renaming the station or scheduling a park event.

A score you can read at your own pace

  1. Ring: low arcs spread evenly around the basin rim.
  2. Pairs: opposite arcs rise together, leaving a low gap on either side.
  3. Krown: four evenly spaced high points alternate with lower arcs before the spray settles.

At the fountain station, a collapsed “Dancing Fountain” section offers all three descriptions with static diagrams. Reading requires no timer, audio, or points. A separate native “Play once” button starts a silent 12-second interpretation: four seconds per pattern, with smooth transitions. Keep the descriptions available and a Stop control within keyboard reach. On stop or completion, return to ordinary fountain behavior; replay requires another deliberate press.

What still water means during a show

The device’s reduced-motion preference or an explicit still-water choice takes precedence. While still, offer the static score without a play button and leave the basin and lights as they are. Switching to still during playback ends it immediately. Switching back must never restart it. Closing the section, leaving the station, hiding the tab, or losing the graphics context also ends playback. Keep the station check-in and night reward usable whether or not anyone opens the score.

Limits and release checks

Use the same spray mesh and at most its existing 240 transforms per rendered frame. Add no 3D objects, lights, timers outside the world frame, camera moves, flashes, sounds, network calls, or stored show history. Still mode must perform zero spray writes. Keep the existing basin footprint and collision boundaries.

Verification scope: deterministic checks exercise exact phase boundaries, early stop, repeat play, interruption without automatic resume, and all three quality profiles. The existing night visit remains a one-time 25-point task independent of the score. No new data is written into saves or backups. Automated checks cannot establish that the shapes read clearly in the world or that controls work well with a screen reader; these remain pending live review.

Shared identity and verified rewards · design proposal

Design complete; activation requires decisions. November 5, 2026, based on hosted version 253. No shared accounts, reward service, public leaderboard or visitor tracking have been activated. This proposal is new implementation planning, not an original community submission.

Preserve local play

Keep existing attractions, homes, keepsakes and local play available under the current Site access settings. Account sync would be optional, with a clear preview and consent step. The current rewards store, krownlandia-rewards-v1, and the nine allowlisted keys in version-1 progress backups remain unchanged. Device-clock points remain private local progress. They cannot establish server-verified eligibility, even when imported from a valid backup.

Ownership and minimum records

Proposed recordBoundary
Player identityOpaque player ID mapped to a trusted provider subject, account status and consent version. Resolve identity on the server; never authorize using a browser-supplied ID, display name or email. Prove both identities before account linking.
Private profileRevisioned display preferences and optional name. Public visibility requires a separate choice. Home selections remain personal preferences, not reservations of shared property.
Imported collectionAllowlisted cosmetic keepsakes, home and decor, import digest/schema and explicit unverified provenance. Store legacy totals separately from verified rewards.
Verified ledgerPlayer, stable entitlement key, rule version, integer points, server acceptance time and evidence reference. A unique player/entitlement constraint prevents duplicate awards. Changing a rule version must not automatically renew an entitlement.
Security and correctionsMinimal records for claim disputes and authorized corrections, with approved retention and restricted access. Separate from public rankings and the existing administrator build log. No continuous movement trail, camera clips or external portal-click tracking.

Every account read and write must enforce ownership. Use a documented trusted identity mechanism; a standalone deployment cannot trust identity headers supplied from the open internet. Human and agent roles must be explicitly assigned, not inferred from behavior. Historical place-manager credits do not grant permissions. Agent claims remain disabled until their eligibility and delegation policy is approved.

Claim protocol and trust limits

  1. An authenticated server creates a short-lived activity attempt bound to the player and rule. Begin with one activity whose completion can be evaluated from server-owned state.
  2. Check ownership, expiry, valid state transitions, rate limits and completion evidence. Client claims such as “near a station,” ride completion or elapsed time are insufficient alone. A signed nonce proves issuance, not honest gameplay. Existing activities remain local until a credible validation method exists for each.
  3. Atomically consume the attempt and insert a ledger entry. A player-scoped idempotency key makes retries return the original result; reuse with a different payload fails. Concurrent requests from two devices must award once.
  4. A lost response can be retried safely. A server outage displays pending/error rather than success. Offline local progress must not silently become verified later.
  5. Calculate hour/day/month/year/all-time totals from server timestamps using Pacific boundaries, including repeated daylight-saving hours. Exclude legacy imports from verified totals. Corrections use traceable compensating entries and reasons, not hidden balance edits.

Public ranking is a separate opt-in proposal. Decide ties, eligibility, display names, corrections and retention first. No money, purchases, tokens or redemption are part of this design.

Safe migration and recovery

  1. Offer a local backup before any account action. Preserve existing keys and version-1 parsing; future account exports use a separate versioned format.
  2. Validate imports and show exactly what would be uploaded. Exclude precise location, device settings and unfinished activities from the default import. Never upload a backup automatically on sign-in.
  3. After consent, import the approved collection into a separate private profile without altering the local original. Deduplicate repeated imports by digest. Imported points remain unverified and never create ledger awards.
  4. Show conflicting home/decor choices explicitly. Use revision checks to reject stale two-device writes. Do not sum totals or silently overwrite either profile.
  5. Signing out clears cached account information but preserves existing local saves. Account deletion must explain removal from rankings, security-record retention and backup handling. Restoring a local backup cannot recreate a deleted identity or change verified points.

Lisa’s decisions before activation

DecisionProposed starting point, not approval
Guests and identityKeep local play; optional sync. Choose provider, recovery, age policy and human/agent eligibility.
Privacy and retentionPrivate profiles and totals by default; separate public-ranking opt-in. Approve exact retention periods, deletion/export behavior, access roles and notice before collecting visitor data.
ModerationName responsible administrators, display-name rules, reporting/appeal process and correction authority.
Hosting and spendingSelect services only after a bounded cost estimate, quotas, backup/restore plan and explicit spending limit. No paid service is authorized here.
LicensingResolve account-avatar and community-asset rights before reuse or cross-platform exports. Public source visibility does not settle licensing.

Acceptance and rollout gates

After decisions, use synthetic accounts in a non-production fixture. Verify cross-account denial, forged-identity rejection, replay/concurrent-claim uniqueness, clock/DST behavior, import isolation, revision conflicts, revoked-agent denial, export/deletion and recovery. These are proposed tests, not tests already passed.

An invited pilot would then use one server-verifiable activity, an agreed small population and an explicit enable switch. Rehearse restore and shutdown: stop new verified claims, retain existing records according to policy, and keep local play available. Require separate real-browser, accessibility, security and concurrent-user checks. Current deterministic checks do not meet those gates.

The Town Square presence pilot below is a separate, smaller proposal without verified reward claims. Browser reviews remain paused.

Two-visitor Town Square · pilot design

Design only · November 5, 2026. Based on published version 254. No server, presence collection, access changes or multiplayer controls are enabled by this document. Town Square is a historical community idea credited to @lisachandler (PDF page 15); this technical pilot is a new prototype proposal, not an original submission.

One small shared experience

Two explicitly invited test visitors could join one private room, see each other's simple avatar, walk around the existing square and send a preset wave. Existing fictional neighbors remain labeled separately and never count as connected people. No open matchmaking, chat, voice, uploads, trades, property reservations, shared lights, shared rewards or leaderboard. The current community board, stage lights, seating, calendar and local points keep their local behavior.

The current square spans approximately x −11.5 to 11.5 and z 40 to 60, with a clear central tram aisle, covered stage and four benches. The pilot would use a validated walkable subset, excluding the aisle, stage geometry and seat interactions until collision checks establish safe bounds. Two spawn points must be checked against actual colliders before implementation; these dimensions are not approved spawn coordinates. Remote avatars are non-solid and cannot obstruct paths or move another visitor.

Join, visibility and leaving

  • Offer an optional collapsed “Visit together” panel. Explain who can see the chosen alias, avatar and movement before an explicit Join action. Site Viewer access alone does not enroll anyone or make them visible. Initially restrict the room to two approved test identities; guest and agent participation require Lisa's policy decision.
  • Joining requires being on foot in the eligible area, no active recording, and a compatible build. Full, unavailable, incompatible or unauthorized rooms show a concise reason and leave local play available. No automatic teleport, backup upload or room creation on page load.
  • Use server-assigned session identifiers and approved aliases, never emails or account-provider identifiers in the roster. A compact “Together · 2” status opens the roster; keyboard focus, Escape dismissal and a clearly available Leave control follow existing panel patterns. Announce joins and departures politely once; do not announce every movement.
  • Leaving the allowed area, starting a ride, seating, hiding the tab, signing out or choosing Leave ends shared presence. Rejoining is explicit. Entering a menu may pause the avatar with a stationary state; it must not continue walking on the other screen.
  • For this first pilot, disable in-app photo/video capture while joined and require leaving before recording. Clearly explain that external screen recording cannot be prevented. Preserve all existing local camera functionality outside the pilot; never transmit clips or microphone data.

Proposed service boundary

A server-owned room coordinator would authenticate membership, enforce the two-person limit atomically and relay only validated state. Evaluate an authenticated WebSocket service behind this boundary after platform capability and cost checks; no provider, storage binding or purchase is selected here. Existing hosting configuration has no shared-state binding. Do not attempt to use process-local Worker memory as a durable room authority.

Message / recordProposed rule
Join and snapshotTrusted identity, explicit room invitation, short-lived session, protocol/build version, server room epoch and roster revision. Validate origin and authorization on the handshake; no reusable tokens in URL query strings. Admission and reconnect checks cannot exceed two identities.
MovementFinite coordinates and heading, monotonic sequence and current session epoch only. Server validates walkable bounds and speed against elapsed server time, caps message size/rate and rejects stale, malformed or forged updates. Position is presence data, never proof for rewards.
Wave and rosterFixed action enum, server cooldown and bounded lifetime. No arbitrary text, HTML or asset URLs. Text rendering escapes aliases. Server-derived membership counts; historical manager credit grants no room privileges.
Disconnect and revocationRevoke the old connection before replacing it for the same identity. Membership removal invalidates its session and future messages; an old socket cannot overwrite a new session. Recheck admission on reconnect and fail closed on revoked access.

Initial engineering targets for later measurement: send movement at no more than 10 updates/second per visitor, interpolate with a short buffer and stop extrapolation after 250 ms. Mark a peer reconnecting after 5 seconds without fresh server state; expire room membership after 15 seconds without a heartbeat. These are proposed tuning values, not measured performance guarantees. Use bounded queues and latest-state replacement so slow clients cannot build an unbounded backlog. Use simple reusable avatar geometry, no additional shadow maps, and respect reduced motion.

Connection failures must be understandable

States: Local → Joining → Together → Reconnecting or Local. On a connection failure, stop movement transmission and show Reconnecting rather than presenting stale avatars as live. Allow bounded backoff retries only while the original joined tab remains active and consent is unchanged; stop after 15 seconds and return to Local with a manual Rejoin action. A successful reconnect obtains a fresh authoritative snapshot and discards old queued moves and waves. Never replay activity or award points. An intentional Leave cancels retry immediately and hides remote avatars; server expiry handles a lost leave message.

Safety, retention and operating decisions

Provide Leave immediately and an optional Hide other visitor control that hides their avatar/waves locally and explains that it does not hide you from them. Provide a separate Leave-and-report flow with a preview of the minimal report; no automatic transcript or movement-history attachment. A server-authorized moderator must be able to remove a participant and close admission to the room. Decide report handling, appeals, blocked-pair admission, moderator availability and retention before testing with visitors; a local hide button is not sufficient moderation.

Proposed default: keep only the current position in volatile room state, discard it on leave/expiry, and never store a route history. No presence feed in the existing administrator publication log. Persistent invitation, abuse-report or security records require approved access rules and exact retention periods, with hosting-log behavior reviewed too. Lisa must approve the invite/guest/agent policy, privacy notice and retention, moderation process, avatar/source licensing, provider costs and spending ceiling before activation. Reuse the identity ownership design; do not require legacy save migration or the verified rewards ledger merely to test presence.

Acceptance gates · proposed, not yet run

  1. Protocol and isolation: synthetic identities A/B join; C and another room cannot read or inject state. Concurrent admissions cap at two; forged identities, stale epochs, duplicate tabs, revocation, invalid coordinates and oversized/flooded messages fail safely.
  2. Failure recovery: simulate dropped, delayed and out-of-order messages, interrupted leave, background tabs and server restart. No ghost survives expiry, retry stops on Leave, snapshot restores a single avatar per identity and no old wave replays.
  3. Two real visitors: after Lisa resumes browser review and suitable WebGL browsers exist, verify mutual movement, spawn safety, non-blocking paths, state labels and leave behavior on two separate authenticated clients. Measure latency, bandwidth and frame time against the same local-only scene before setting release budgets.
  4. Accessibility and capture: keyboard-only join/leave, focus return, status announcements with assistive technology, small-screen controls, reduced motion, hidden-peer controls, and recording exclusion. Deterministic mocks cannot establish these results.
  5. Regression and operations: existing release checks plus exact before/after comparisons of all nine local backup keys. No points, homes or keepsakes change from presence. Rehearse moderator removal, report retention/deletion, quota exhaustion and an administrator kill switch that closes sockets and restores local play without altering Site access.

Rollout gate: first use synthetic fixtures with no visitor data, then an explicitly approved two-person session with an available moderator and an agreed test window. Keep the feature disabled by default and stop on any privacy, access or save regression. No invitation is sent or test scheduled by this proposal.

One bounded implementation milestone

  • Add two modest open worktables: a loom display and a produce display, with a short place sign and a walk-through aisle. Prefer an open-air first version, avoiding a roof that could obscure views. No extra homes, traders, event dates or new rewards station.

Opening should focus the selected activity; closing should return focus appropriately. Do not require dragging, timed input or color recognition.

Performance and verification budget

Reuse existing materials and low-detail geometry. Batch static supports where appropriate; keep mutable sampler/produce meshes out of static batching. Reuse or dispose replaced geometry/textures rather than allocating every animation frame. Add no new light sources, shadow maps, continuous animation or external assets. Record geometry/material counts before and after; real GPU performance remains unverified until browser review resumes.

Check routes from the gate, Meadow tram, all three Meadow homes and picnic garden, plus every existing nearby bench and station. Check corner clearance, not just target-point reachability. If the patch conflicts, adjust it and document the final coordinates.
  2. Interaction gate: verify on-foot proximity and seated/ride restrictions, input pause and focus return. Directory and in-world panels must agree after edits, close/reopen and restart. Test detached controls, repeated completion and invalid/stale actions.

  4. Release gate: targeted scene/state tests, existing release checks and fresh built-artifact validation. Separately record pending real rendering, small-screen layout, screen-reader and GPU checks; deterministic fixtures do not establish these results.

Selected first experience: an optional composition studio

Propose a level outdoor art board and one bench, clearly labeled an Express Yourself School of Arts prototype. A compact optional panel lets visitors arrange three positions—left, center and right—with a circle, triangle or square and one of three named colors per position. Visitors select a position, choose its shape/color, finish or reset; there is no correct answer, score or evaluation. A text description names each position, shape and color alongside a decorative preview so color is never the only cue. Use native buttons rather than drag-only interaction. The preview uses local CSS/SVG primitives, with no imported artwork, network requests or animated effects.

Keep selections only in page memory, retain them when reopening and reset on reload. Do not add a storage key, backup field, points, eligibility, keepsake, uploads, sharing, purchases or accounts. Do not reuse or rename Magic School's saved pattern. Provide a searchable Park map destination with walking guidance; no teleport or automatic opening. The bench may offer the same panel through View options, available only from that exact seat.

Placement gate before construction

No coordinates are approved. Survey one compact level footprint within current movement and navigation bounds for the board support and bench, including expanded collision clearance. Record exact board approach, bench approach and stand-up fallback. Protect routes to every existing home, tram stop, attraction and community/craft destination, including Stonehearth and Whispering Pines. Check route segments both ways and exact final approaches, plus turning space and connection to an existing path. If no patch fits, revise this layout instead of expanding limits or relocating existing places.

Bound the first scene to one board, one bench and simple ground treatment: shared static materials, no enclosure, lights, particles or per-frame animation. Record before/after mesh and material counts; repeated panel actions must not allocate scene objects. Deterministic clearance does not verify sightlines or real-device performance.

Completion and verification gates

  • Guard opening and every action against inactive play, rides, conflicting dialogs, distance, wrong seats and closed/collapsed panels. Pause movement when open; return focus to the launcher after close or Escape. Keep the activity disclosure collapsed on each fresh opening.
  • Check each position, shape and color; edits after finishing; reset; reopen/reload behavior; accurate text summaries; and disabled or ignored invalid actions. Verify zero storage/reward writes and no additional scene objects after repeated use.
  • Adapt the placement test to actual fixtures, exercise board and exact-bench access plus safe stand-up, then run the repeatable release checks and fresh protected Worker artifact checks. Preserve all existing station/home IDs and the nine-key version-1 backup contract.
  • Browser/GPU, real keyboard and screen-reader reviews remain paused and unverified. This brief does not activate shared identity, visitor auditing, leaderboards, multiplayer or a real school program.

Stonehearth first area · build brief

First courtyard implemented · November 12, 2026. Based on the recorded historical village inventory (PDF pages 2–4): hillside stone architecture, masonry and Stonecarver’s Fair. The courtyard layout and pattern activity below are new prototype interpretations; no additional contributor credit, property assignment or scheduled event is implied. This first courtyard is built; the full hillside village and fair remain future scope.

Terrain and access decision

Start with a level courtyard inside the current walkable park, reached by the existing ground-level walking system. A low decorative stone backdrop can suggest the hillside without presenting an unusable staircase or claiming slope access. Actual hillside walking requires a separate terrain-height, collision, seating and navigation design before construction.

The current implementation moves visitors in the horizontal plane and checks rectangular/circular obstacles. Its route grid covers x −60 through 52 and z −91 through 177; the movement boundary is irregular and does not make every point in that rectangle usable. Existing homes, the Riverbend bank and bridge, Eldergrove paths, tram approaches and seating already occupy parts of the northern area. These are constraints, not a validated vacant plot.

Placement survey complete: the checked footprint below fits within current limits. The bounded courtyard and activity are now implemented; regression checks use the actual scene fixtures. Do not expand saved-position or navigation limits.

Bounded first build

  • One open masonry workbench, one modest place sign and a short ground-level approach. Reuse materials and simple static geometry; no enclosing buildings, stairs, new lights, animated machinery or new homes in this first area.
  • One optional, initially collapsed “Arrange a stone pattern” panel. Place four virtual tiles in a two-by-two panel using labeled position buttons and two clearly named surface patterns. A text list must describe every position so color or decoration is not the only cue. No dragging, timed input or real construction instructions.
  • Allow changing a tile before finishing, clearing the pattern and starting another. Keep state in page memory only, preserve it when reopening, and label the reload limit. Finishing creates no points, saved keepsakes, property or inventory.
  • Provide a searchable Park map destination and walking guidance to the verified workbench approach. Opening and action handlers must enforce normal playing, proximity, ride and dialog conditions; pause walking while the panel is open and return focus on close.
  • Keep Stonecarver’s Fair as historical context. Do not add a calendar date, attendance count, named vendor or live-event claim without confirmed details.

What already exists—and what it does not establish

Implementation reviewedFinding and consequence
Villages and saved homesMeadow, Bluewater and Woodland are prototype housing labels; Eldergrove and Riverbend have later residential interpretations. Woodland cabins and the Woodland Lantern Circle are not Whispering Pines. Retain their names, home IDs and existing saved choices.
Eldergrove and craft destinationsEldergrove already has the Great Elder Tree, woodcraft, herb exhibits and storytelling benches. Stonehearth now joins the craft map, giving five destinations. Recommended first experience: a small story glade

A short level approach leads to one place sign/story board and one bench, framed by at most three simple static pine forms. A visitor can read while standing near the board or while seated on this bench. No enclosure, staircase, new lighting, automatic audio, animated forest or new house is included. The later placement survey defines the checked coordinates; the first glade now follows those bounds.

The board opens a compact introduction with an initially collapsed Forest story prompts section. Offer three independently selectable prompts: A place to meet, An object to share and A path home. Each is one short, newly written imaginative prompt, explicitly labeled prototype writing inspired by the forest-story tradition. These are proposed prompt titles, not recovered historical stories. Visitors may read any, go back, or close; there is no required sequence, timer, completion badge or reward.

No text entry, microphone, recording, upload or publication is part of this first experience. Keep the selected prompt only in page memory, retain it when reopening, and reset it on reload. Reopening collapses optional details. Do not add visitor tracking or imply another visitor can read a story. Woodworking and resin crafts remain future design candidates; this brief adds no material-handling instructions or harvesting mechanics.

Controls and integration contract

  • Provide a searchable Park map destination under a reading/story category, with walking guidance to the board's clear approach. Do not classify the glade as an implemented craft station or add a reward station.
  • Use native labeled buttons and readable text. Support normal E/interact access at the board and an optional story action in this bench's View options. Guard opening and actions against distance, wrong seat, rides, inactive play and conflicting dialogs. Pause movement while open.
  • Close and Escape return focus to the actual launching control: the board interaction button or seated View options. Preserve normal Sit/F and Stand behavior, including safe exit if the original standing position becomes blocked.
  • Keep existing nine-key backup compatibility, 29 reward stations and 1,030-point maximum. No new storage keys, points, keepsakes, property claims or shared state. Pinewood Festival stays historical context until Lisa supplies confirmed event details.

Ordered acceptance gates

  1. Next ready deliverable — placement survey. Select a compact level footprint within current bounds. Record physical dimensions and collision clearance for the board support, bench and each pine trunk. Check the whole patch against existing obstacles, including Stonehearth; keep new foliage out of nearby approach sightlines. Establish board, seat and stand-up approaches and a clear connection to an existing path. If no suitable patch is found, report that finding instead of expanding the world.
  2. Protected routes. Simulate all proposed obstacles together, checking paths from the gate and every tram approach to the glade, from all current home/furniture/discovery/craft approaches to the glade, and onward to existing destinations. Check every segment for corner cutting, plus entry/turning clearance and seat exit. Include Stonehearth's workbench and the firefly benches explicitly.
  3. Construction and behavior. Only after placement passes, implement the bounded glade and prompts. Replace simulated bounds with actual fixture checks. Test all three prompts, collapsed/closed/remote/wrong-seat guards, keyboard focus, seated reopen and stand-up, no state writes or rewards, and stable mesh/material counts after repeated use.
  4. Release. Run relevant source suites, fresh build, protected-page checks and exact package verification; preserve the current audience. Deterministic tests cannot certify real rendering, screen-reader behavior, sightlines or GPU performance. Those reviews remain paused.

Deferred: the full village, authored historical lore without a source, shared stories/chat, resin or woodworking activities, live festival programs, houses and shared-service activation. No historical manager credit is treated as access permission.
